output.decision: Add the shaker cup to shipment #3. It is complementary to creatine rather than additional creatine, which directly avoids worsening the observed “too much product” cancellation reason. Send a shipment-specific pre-billing reminder that foregrounds the gift, states the upcoming charge and shipment plainly, and offers a one-click delay before account-management options. Suggested copy: “Your third creatine delivery is coming soon—and we’re including a complimentary shaker cup. Your subscription will renew on [DATE] for [AMOUNT] and ship around [SHIP DATE]. Need more time to finish what you have? Delay this delivery here: [DELAY LINK]. You can also manage your subscription here: [MANAGE LINK].”
next_steps: Confirm shaker-cup inventory, unit cost, pack-out method, and whether it fits all shipment destinations.
Configure eligibility for active creatine subscribers’ third paid subscription order only, excluding prior recipients if applicable.
Build a shipment-#3 billing reminder using dynamic renewal date, amount, shipment date, delay link, and manage link.
Place the delay option above the manage-subscription link; keep cancellation/account controls accessible rather than hidden.
QA the reminder and fulfillment rule with test subscriptions before launch.
missing_inputs: Billing lead time and the exact renewal versus shipment date customers should see.
Whether the shaker cup has destination, inventory, or fulfillment constraints.
Available subscription-platform capabilities for one-click delay links and order-number segmentation.
Brand-approved product-benefit language, sender voice, and legal/compliance review requirements.

evidence_used.supports: Advises against gifting more of the subscribed product when excess inventory is a cancellation driver, and recommends communicating an upcoming gift in a customized billing reminder.
Recommends presenting a delay option for customers with too much product and customizing reminders by subscription order number.

assumptions: The shaker cup is useful with creatine and does not materially increase the customer’s excess consumable inventory.
Shipment #3 refers to the third recurring subscription order, not the customer’s third lifetime purchase of any kind.
The brand can accurately segment third-order creatine subscribers and include the cup in fulfillment.
The proposed message is a practical template; required disclosures and timing should be validated for the brand’s markets.
